cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1,047 women with intrapartum fever from a total of 24,784 deliveries at a tertiary center between 2019 and 2021.
finding: The developed nomogram provides a clinically useful tool to predict delivery mode and NICU admission in women with intrapartum fever, with the cesarean delivery model achieving an AUC of 0.8 (training) and 0.783 (testing), and the NICU admission model achieving AUC of 0.681 (training) and 0.748 (testing).
mod_finding: Predictors of cesarean delivery included advanced maternal age, hypertensive disorders, Intrapartum Antibiotic Prophylaxis (IAP), Meconium-Stained Amniotic Fluid (MSAF), Macrosomia, Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH), Oligohydramnios, assisted reproductive technology (ART), Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy (HDP), Maternal tachycardia, Placental histopathology, intrapartum temperature and Method of inducing labor.
birth_weight: Macrosomia and Low Birth Weight (LBW) were identified as predictors for study outcomes.
